newsitem.title: SPAIN: Argentaria agrees slimdown of troubled unit.
newsitem.headline: Argentaria agrees slimdown of troubled unit.

text.p: Spanish bank Argentaria said on Thursday it had agreed with unions a plan to slim down the staff of its troubled Banco Exterior unit.

Trade unions Workers Commission (CCOO) and General Trade Union (UGT) agreed on early retirements for 1,500 workers at 85 percent of wages and incentives for a further 600 workers to retire early, Argentaria said in a statement.
This would bring the bank's staff down to 4,500 from 6,600 by the year 2000.
BEX said it would cover the cost of the plan with shareholders reserves, currently standing above 50 billion pesetas ($325 million).

"From now on the bank is beginning a new phase... in which BEX will be a key part of the (Argentaria) group that improves profitability and faces tough sector competition as an independent and private bank," Argentaria said in a statement.

Argentaria, still 29.2 percent state-owned and due for further privatisation, presented its restructuring plan for BEX, considered its key weakness, in early May and has since been negotiating with unions.

Argentaria, formed in 1991 in a merger of six state-owned banks and savings banks, embarked last year on an aggressive campaign to boost sagging profitability by restructuring assets and liabilities and expanding a small domestic network.
The BEX group earned 7.26 billion pesetas in 1996, up from 5.94 billion. Total assets dropped to 5.42 trillion from 6.64 trillion. ($ = 153.5 Spanish Pesetas)
